scope: Offline log and preserved checkpoint coverage only; no server/inference/rollout
normalization_limits: Components divided by configured weight remove multiplicative weight only; episode reward accumulation/reset/normalization can differ from stepwise kernel mean.
Exponential reward cannot be inverted into aggregate RMSE; Jensen and episode weighting prevent this.
Error_vel_xy/yaw logger metrics are training command tracking summaries; current source body was not recovered and these are not fixed heldout RMSE/MAE.
Timeout/base_contact are logged training termination fractions, not official survival probability.
Earlier/later checkpoints experience changing curriculum/commands, unequal trajectory distribution and stochastic training actions.
No independent training seed, no heldout evaluation; no official score mapping.

checkpoint1000_vs1499.comparison: checkpoint1000 and1499 each preceding50 logged iterations; training distribution is not fixed

local_reward_semantics_source.limitation: Historical local source; current B1 params cite identical function names/std0.5 but current runtime function body and reward-manager logging normalization are not recovered.

interpretation: Initial learning is substantial; XY logger error improves to around0.7 by600 then mostly plateaus.
Late1500 can handle a higher curriculum level than600 while maintaining comparable XY, but training base-contact termination increases and yaw logger error worsens relative600.
1499 vs1000 offers about4.9% lower XY and2.0% lower yaw logger errors with1.263 percentage-point higher base-contact fraction; this is a tradeoff, not a measured heldout gain.
A total-reward best checkpoint600 is influenced by easier curriculum and different sample distribution; it cannot be called evaluation-best.
No evidence here supports assigning a total score or claiming a large official improvement; baseline comparisons require same-condition rollout, which was not run.
